title: Staged precision guardrail orchestrator for FP8/INT8 calibration
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a staged 'precision guardrail' orchestrator that automates calibration, accuracy validation, and traffic steering for FP8/INT8 candidate builds and automatically falls back to a safe variant when quality gates fail.

Background: We've been shipping quantized variants (INT8 and experimental FP8) to reduce token cost. Current rollouts are manual and require engineers to interpret offline calibration reports and run ad-hoc canaries. That increases risk: silent quality regressions reach production or rollouts are slowed by manual gating. This ticket builds an orchestrator that ties together calibration jobs, evaluation harnesses, canary traffic routing, runtime health checks, and automatic safe switchover policies.

Scope:
- Define canonical calibration workflow for FP8/INT8 profiles (data sampling, per-layer stats collection, range/scale selection).
- Integrate with existing calibration harness to produce a compact quant-profile artifact and calibration metadata (seed, corpus snapshot, profile id).
- Run automated accuracy validation against a curated eval set (prompt families + business-critical prompt seeds) and compute guarded metrics (delta perplexity, EM/ROUGE-style thresholds, response-quality heuristics).
- Launch a staged canary: start at 1% traffic with mirrored validation traffic and metric collection, then escalate to 5/25% on green signals.
- Implement automated fallback: if any safety or quality gate breaches (statistical significance + monotonic degradation of key prompts) within the canary window or during early ramp, steer traffic to the pinned safe variant (FP16 or pre-quantized INT8 verified build) and create an incident ticket.
- Expose observability: per-profile dashboards, alerting rules, and a reconciliation log for audit.

Non-goals: automated retraining, model architecture changes, end-user UI redesign for Console (but we will emit hooks that Console can pick up).
acceptance_criteria: Calibration workflow produces deterministic quant-profile artifacts with unique profile-id and source-corpus hash
Automated eval run produces a pass/fail decision based on configurable thresholds (default: max 1.5% EM regression or configurable absolute delta) and stores the metrics in the metrics store
Canary controller can programmatically allocate traffic percentages to a quantized variant and mirror 100% of validation traffic to the quantized path without affecting user latency SLA
Automatic fallback triggers within the canary window and returns 100% of affected traffic to the safe variant when guarded metrics breach thresholds
Audit log contains timestamped events for calibration, validation, canary start/stop, fallback decision, and operator acknowledgements
testing_plan:
1) End-to-end unit: run calibration on sample models (llama-2-7b, open-llama-13b) to produce profiles and verify artifact format.
2) Offline evaluation: run eval harness against curated prompt set; validate metrics computation and threshold logic.
3) Synthetic canary: use local cluster to route 1% synthetic traffic and assert mirrored traces appear; verify fallback triggers when we inject a synthetic metric breach.
4) Staged prod pilot: 1% -> 5% -> 25% with close monitoring; run kill-switch to simulate failure and ensure automatic switchover completes in <30s and preserves request integrity.
5) Chaos tests: introduce higher tail latencies and KV cache misses to validate that fallback does not cascade to unrelated routes.
rollout_plan: Feature branch + unit tests merged to runtime-quantization
Integration test job in CI generating sample profiles and storing artifacts in staging bucket
Canary run in staging with synthetic traffic and validation dashboard visible to SRE
Gradual production pilot with 1% traffic for 48h, monitor metrics and alerts
On success, escalate to 5% for 24h then 25% for 48h; rollback automatically if gates fail
observability:
Metrics: quant.profile_pass_rate, quant.per_prompt_delta_{metric}, quant.canary_failure_count, quant.fallback_count.
Dashboards: per-profile time-series (delta vs baseline), distribution of prompt-level deltas, end-to-end latency P50/P95.
Alerts: alert on quant.fallback_count>0 (pager), alert on per_prompt_delta exceeding threshold for >10 minutes (pager), warn for anomalous drift in rolling 7-day baseline (email).
implementation_notes:
Design decisions: use the existing calibration harness codepath but introduce a lightweight profile metadata JSON that includes sampling seed and corpus hash to ensure reproducibility. We'll prefer a conservative default quantization map (per-channel symmetric for INT8, calibrated FP8 scales where supported).
Trade-offs: aggressive quantization reduces cost but increases risk of prompt-level degradation; we will bias initial defaults to minimize false positives for fallback while surfacing per-prompt deltas for product owners.
Runtime behavior: orchestrator will call runtime traffic-router API to adjust weights; fallback uses single-step full-traffic switch to safe variant plus a safety window that prevents immediate re-roll to the same profile for 24h unless manually approved.
Security: profile artifacts stored in customer bucket for private deployments must be encrypted and KMS-tagged (hooked to existing KMS integrations).
